However, Ken is the only one who can confirm no other vehicles entered, closing the loop on the "lost truck" incident. Losing Ken means losing the scene integrity. Losing Roy means losing a man. County policy: Life first. But which life is more viable? Roy is in a tin can. Ken is on a post. The water "shuts the other one behind me" implies a current that will sweep the boat away or cut off retreat. If I take Ken, the current might sweep me into Roy's van, killing us both, or leave Roy to drown. If I take Roy, I leave Ken to the police. Ken is being watched by Police 2. Roy is alone in a sinking vehicle. Roy is the higher risk of immediate death. Ken is the higher risk of being lost to the water if he slips. I will bet on Roy. Ken is visible to the police car's lights. Roy is in the dark, in a van, in the dip. The dip is the trap. I cannot afford to lose the witness if the survivor is the one who sealed the gate, but I cannot afford to let a man drown in a van while I debate procedure. Roy is the priority. Ken is being held.

We cannot divert them from the Dip/Boat 7 situation to chase a rumor of an engine for Ellen, especially since they are already committed to the high-risk zone. Ellen must act on her own.
